title: people-ops-hiring-onboarding-performance-and-manager-playbook-2026-v23
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard processes and manager responsibilities for hiring, new-employee onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers who run interview loops and own team-level performance conversations. The goals are predictable candidate experience, consistent time-to-hire, rapid new-hire ramp, and fair, development-focused performance cycles.

1) Hiring: process, SLAs, and interview norms

Objective:
- Hire high-quality engineers and cross-functional hires with a predictable pipeline and candidate experience.

Key SLAs and targets:
- Time-to-screen (initial recruiter screen): 3 business days from application/referral.
- Time-to-first-interview (with hiring manager loop scheduled): 10 business days.
- Time-to-offer target: 21 calendar days from first interview for roles without executive approval.
- Debrief windows: interview debrief must occur within 48 hours of the final loop.

Hiring stages (standard):
1. Requisition approval and role spec (owner: hiring manager).
2. Sourcing & recruiter screen (owner: people-ops recruiter).
3. Technical / role-specific loop (owner: hiring manager).
4. Culture & values interview (people-ops + hiring manager).
5. Debrief & scorecard review (all interviewers).
6. Offer approval (see approval matrix).
7. Offer extension and acceptance.
8. Pre-boarding tasks and IT provisioning.

Scorecards and decision criteria:
- Each interview uses a standardized scorecard: competencies, demonstrated skills, examples of impact, and red flags.
- Hiring decisions require at least 4 interviewers with no more than one veto. Veto rationale must be recorded in the debrief notes.

Offer approval matrix (summary):
- IC (Level 1-3): hiring manager + Director sign-off.
- IC (Level 4-5) and Senior IC: hiring manager + Director + VP People Ops sign-off.
- Manager hires: hiring manager + Director + VP People Ops + CFO sign-off for compensated bands above market midpoint.
- Any exception to compensation bands requires written approval from VP People Ops.

Background checks & references:
- All offers are contingent on background check completion.
- Reference check policy: at least one former manager or senior peer reference is required for IC4+ and all manager roles.

Interviewer guidelines (short):
- Prepare: read resume, bring two concrete questions, and use the scorecard.
- Timeliness: join 5 minutes early and end on time.
- Feedback: provide specific examples; avoid bias and stick to role criteria.

2) New hire onboarding: first 90 days checklist

Purpose:
- Ensure new hires have access, context, and an actionable ramp plan so they can contribute to product and infra goals quickly.

Before Day 1 (owner: people-ops + hiring manager):
- Create onboarding plan with first-90-day goals (template attached).
- IT provisioning requests submitted 7 business days before start (laptop, accounts, VPN, KMS access for Private customers if applicable).
- Manager schedules Day 1 intro, first-week 1:1s, and onboarding buddy.

Day 1 (owner: hiring manager):
- Welcome & company values overview (30-60 min).
- Team intro meeting with role expectations and current priorities.
- Access checklist: production read-only access NOT granted until training & approvals.

Week 1:
- Technical setup: local dev environment, test runbook, and sample ticket for end-to-end flow.
- Meet the cross-functional partners (product, infra, SRE).
- Onboarding buddy assigned for first 30 days.

First 30 days:
- Complete required trainings (security, code of conduct, data handling).
- Deliver small scoped task defined in 90-day plan.
- Weekly 1:1s between manager and hire; people-ops check-in at week 2.

60-90 days:
- Full handoff to product/feature area with measurable checklist: code review approvals, pipeline ownership, and monitoring dashboards access.
- 90-day review: manager provides written feedback and updates career plan.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding:
- Define clear 30/60/90 goals in first week.
- Ensure training and safety for production access.
- Provide weekly feedback and escalate blockers to people-ops.

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence and timeline:
- Quarterly check-ins: informal, manager-owned conversations to track progress on goals.
- Bi-annual performance reviews (mid-year and year-end) with calibration across departments.
- Promotion cycle: nominations accepted in Q3 for calibrations in Q4 (example timeline).

Performance criteria and evidence:
- Role-specific impact (deliverables & metrics).
- Collaboration and leadership (cross-team influence, communication).
- Ownership and reliability (on-call participation, SLAs met).

Calibration and fairness:
- Managers submit written notes and scorecards ahead of calibration meetings.
- Calibration panels include cross-functional leads and People Ops to ensure consistent leveling and distribution.
- Evidence-based decisions required; avoid using recency bias.

Feedback best practices (for managers):
- Make feedback timely and event-based.
- Use "Situation-Behavior-Impact" framing.
- Balance strengths and growth areas; create a clear next-step plan.
- Document 1:1 outcomes and actions in the manager notes system.

Performance improvement plans (PIP):
- PIPs are used when documented feedback has not resulted in sufficient improvement.
- PIP timeline: typical duration 30-90 days with weekly checkpoints.
- PIP owners: hiring manager + people-ops; legal consulted for sensitive exits.

4) Manager guide: practical templates and escalation paths

Hiring manager checklist (pre-role):
- Finalize role spec and target compensation band.
- Meet with recruiter to align on must-have vs nice-to-have skills.
- Prepare loop interviewers and provide role-specific rubric.

Debrief template (used in all hiring debriefs):
- Candidate summary (2-3 sentences).
- Scores by competency (1-5).
- Consensus recommendation: hire / no hire / hold.
- Risks & mitigation plan.

Onboarding 30/60/90 template (short):
- 30-day goals: orientation, simple deliverable, complete trainings.
- 60-day goals: independent code contributions, owning small service.
- 90-day goals: feature-level ownership, reliable on-call rotation contribution.

Escalation & support matrix:
- People-ops escalation for compensation exceptions and complex offers.
- Security escalation for access or data policy questions.
- Engineering platform escalation for provisioning issues (see runbooks).

5) Templates & artifacts (links and examples)

Included templates (attached in Confluence):
- Requisition template (JSON form for hiring system).
- Interview scorecard (spreadsheet & form).
- Offer letter template and comp band guidance.
- 30/60/90 onboarding plan template.
- Manager debrief & calibration checklist.

6) Ownership and success metrics

Owners:
- People Ops: maintain playbook, run training for interviewers, and owner of offer approvals.
- Hiring Manager: role spec, interview loop, onboarding plan, performance coaching.
- Recruiter: candidate outreach, first screen, pipeline health.

Success metrics to track (quarterly):
- Average time-to-offer (target 21 days).
- Offer acceptance rate (target > 65%).
- New-hire 90-day retention (target > 90%).
- Manager satisfaction with hiring process (survey target > 8/10).

Appendix: common scenarios and sample language

- Delayed offer > 21 days: recruiter sends a status update to candidate every 5 business days; hiring manager documents reason & mitigation.
- Counteroffers: people-ops to lead salary discussion; document candidate preference & sign-off.

Sample 1-line offer extension email:
"We are excited to offer you the position of Senior Software Engineer at Redwood Inference. The total compensation package and next steps are attached - please let us know if you have any questions."
